title: Man. Post. Cap. I: Placeus holds Confession vs Pelagians; Chamier three heads; two additions
pass_a_gloss: I hold tightly, and accurately defend, whatever the truly Christian Church has defined of old against the old and new Pelagians and Semipelagians concerning original sin, and in these last ages has professed by her public confessions that she believes. And that whole Daniel Chamier, a man of great name by his own merit among our Churches, establishing the state of the controversy between us and Pighius and Salmeron, has reduced to three heads. Catholics, he says (he understands Protestants), teach by sure arguments that there is in human nature itself a corruption, or pravity proper to each man, other than the acts of sin. Secondly, that the same is in each man even as he is being born. Third, that the same takes its rise from Adam, and by propagation is derived into posterity. Although he subjoins that these three heads contain the whole nature of original sin—and therefore when they are demonstrated nothing will be left remaining—yet for the sake of fuller explanation I will add two things: one, that this corruption has so depraved all the faculties of our soul that unless we have been born again of water and the Spirit, we can neither bring forth any truly good fruit nor be converted to God. The other, that this corruption is truly sin, making all Adam's posterity, Christ alone excepted, in whom it never was, guilty of eternal death.
pass_b_english: I hold fast, and carefully defend, whatever the truly Christian Church has defined against old and new Pelagians and Semipelagians on original sin, and what she has professed in these later ages by her public confessions. Daniel Chamier—a man of deserved name among our churches—reduced the whole dispute between us and Pighius and Salmeron to three heads. Catholics (he means Protestants), he says, prove by sure arguments that human nature itself has a corruption or pravity proper to each person, distinct from sinful acts; second, that the same is in each even at birth; third, that it rises from Adam and passes to posterity by propagation. Though he adds that these three contain the whole nature of original sin—so that once proved nothing remains—I still add two points for clearer teaching: first, that this corruption so spoils every faculty of the soul that, unless we are born again of water and the Spirit, we can neither bear any truly good fruit nor turn to God; second, that this corruption is truly sin, and makes all Adam's posterity—Christ alone excepted, in whom it never was—guilty of eternal death.
source_text: Ego arcte teneo, accurateque defendo quicquid de peccato originali Ecclesia vere Christiana adversus veteres novosque Pelagianos, et Semipelagianos cum definivit olim, tum his postremis seculis suis publicis confessionibus se credere professa est. Id autem universum Daniel Chamierus, vir suo merito magni apud Ecclesias nostras nominis, statum controversiae inter nos et Pighium ac Salmeronem constituens ad tria capita revocavit. Catholici, inquit, (Protestantes intelligit) certis argumentis docent, ipsi humanae naturae inesse corruptionem, seu pravitatem cuilibet homini propriam, aliam ab actibus peccati. Secundo, etiam nascenti homini cuilibet eandem inesse. Tertio eandem ab Adamo ortum ducere, et per propagationem derivari in posteros. Quamvis autem subjungat, haec tria capita continere universam peccati originalis naturam. Itaque iis demonstratis nihil fore reliqui factum; tamen uberioris explicationis causa duo addam: unum, hanc corruptionem omnes animae nostrae facultates ita depravasse, ut nisi ex aqua et Spiritu renati fuerimus, neque ullum fructum vere bonum proferre, neque ad Deum converti valeamus. Alterum, hanc corruptionem vere peccatum esse, omnes Adami posteros, solo Christo, in quo nunquam fuit, excepto, mortis aeternae reos peragens.
